title: The best approximation tuple: an extension of the Cheney-Goldstein algorithm and results to the multiple sets case
summary: We extend the algorithm and several results published in the celebrated 1959 paper of Cheney and Goldstein about the best approximation pair (BAP) problem in two separate directions. One is, for the first time, the ability to consider more than two sets, a task which has been in the mind of researchers for many years without much success in fulfilling it because of a certain theoretical obstacle related to cycles and minimizers of general functionals.
